findings: Bundles improved both screening weeks; 26 shared gigs per week. Bundle+auction adds only87.63 euros mean beyond bundles alone, so do not assume that small difference generalizes.
Broader volume plus bundles raises two-seed mean22.1%, but worsens seed15 from9652.03 euros and98.9% on time to9096.26 euros and93.6%.
Broader volume couples route length, minimum supply, daily capacity and backlog. Many added wins exceed550km. The current study isolates700km routes with original capacity and supply gates.
A separate15-minute hold-only control isolates the effect of matching from posting delay.
Whole-week scores and ledgers reconcile. Shared-gig fee lines have null orderId; individual order margins exclude shared costs and cannot be treated as net bundle profit.

Batch-timing replay on eight old development weeks gives266 pairs at15 minutes versus349 at30. Extra modeled saving is122.19 euros/week; this is not a causal profit forecast and does not yet justify a large timing sweep.
Long-route screen finds36.9 otherwise-feasible requests/week between550–700km and10.4 between700–900km. Dynamic capacity, wins and actual fulfillment remain unmodeled.

Hold-only control ends at6182.61/9323.63 euros. Its mean gain is495.84 euros versus the baseline; route pairing adds232.285 euros beyond the identical posting delay, positive on both screening seeds. Do not attribute all of the bundle treatment gain to matching.
700km-only bundle treatment ends at7407.63/9410.50 euros, minimum96.6% on time. It gains versus the old baseline in both weeks but not versus bundles alone. No900km experiment scheduled.
